# Changelog

All notable changes to InvoicePlane will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Full write-ups for individual vulnerabilities live in the published
[GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories)
and in [`.github/security/`](security/). This changelog records *what* changed; the advisories
record *why* and *how*.

---

### Security fixes

- **Unauthenticated access to the internal `Layout` controller discloses server paths via PHP error backtraces (CWE-200 / CWE-862):** `Layout` extends `MX_Controller` rather than `Admin_Controller`/`Guest_Controller`, so it inherited no authentication gate, and its public methods (`render`, `load_view`, `buffer`, `set`) — meant to be called only internally as `$this->layout->render()` by already-authenticated controllers — were directly HTTP-routable to anonymous clients. Reached unauthenticated, the internal view loader ran with helpers/libraries never autoloaded in that context, raising PHP errors that (with `display_errors` on) disclosed the server's absolute install path and internal file layout to an anonymous attacker, e.g. `GET /layout/load_view/dashboard`. Path-traversal/LFI toward other files was tested and ruled out (Apache's `AllowEncodedSlashes Off` blocks it), so the demonstrated impact is scoped to information disclosure. **Fix:** a `_remap()` on `Layout` now `show_404()`s any direct HTTP route to the controller; the normal internal `$this->layout->render()`/`buffer()`/`set()`/`load_view()` usage is unaffected, since that never goes through HTTP routing. Thanks to [@krishnan-tech](https://github.com/krishnan-tech) for responsible disclosure. [#1809](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1809)

- **Login response-time oracle reveals account existence despite a uniform error message (CWE-208 / CWE-204):** `Sessions::login()` deliberately returns the same generic "credentials incorrect" message for every failed login, but `Mdl_Sessions::auth()` only reached the bcrypt `password_verify()` call when a row for the submitted email existed, returning immediately otherwise. This produced a measurable, reproducible response-time difference (~2x in testing) that revealed whether an email was a registered account, narrowing targets for password-reset abuse, phishing, and credential stuffing. **Fix:** `auth()` now runs a bcrypt comparison against a fixed decoy hash when no account exists, so the non-existent-email path takes about as long as the real one. Thanks to [@krishnan-tech](https://github.com/krishnan-tech) for responsible disclosure. [#1808](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1808)

- **CSRF on logout — a plain GET with no token destroys the session (CWE-352):** `Sessions::logout()` destroyed the session on a plain GET with no CSRF check. Because the session cookie can carry on a top-level cross-site navigation (a link click, `window.location`, a redirect), an attacker page could force an authenticated victim's session to end simply by getting them to navigate to `/sessions/logout`. **Fix:** logout is now a state-changing action like any other in this app — it requires a POST carrying a valid `_csrf_field()` token (checked the same way `Sessions`' own new-password POST already does, since `Sessions` is a `Base_Controller` and cannot call `ensure_valid_post_request()`), and the logout link in the navbar/guest layout is a small same-origin form rather than a plain `<a href>`. Thanks to [@krishnan-tech](https://github.com/krishnan-tech) for responsible disclosure. [#1807](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1807)

- **Admin-gated mail relay: arbitrary recipient and sender spoofing via invoice/quote mailer (CWE-288):** The `send_invoice()` and `send_quote()` endpoints accepted fully attacker-controlled `to_email`, `from_email`, `from_name`, `cc`, and `bcc` parameters, validated only for RFC syntax. An authenticated admin could send branded invoice/quote PDFs from arbitrary sender identities to arbitrary recipient addresses, enabling phishing and data exfiltration. **Fix:** recipient is now bound to the invoice/quote's client email; the From address is pinned to the configured organization email (`smtp_mail_from` setting, or the associated user email as fallback); user-supplied `to_email`/`from_email`/`from_name` are ignored. CC/BCC remain optional but syntax-validated. Form views updated to show read-only recipient/sender info instead of editable fields. Thanks to [@krishnan-tech](https://github.com/krishnan-tech) for responsible disclosure. [#1815](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1815) **Follow-up:** CC and BCC are now restricted to the organisation domain as well (`mailer_internal_domain`, else the sender's domain; `,` and `;` lists; an unknown domain refuses every copy), completing the recipient binding. Thanks again to [@krishnan-tech](https://github.com/krishnan-tech) for responsible disclosure. ([#1831](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1831))

- **Stored XSS via `first_day_of_week` setting (JavaScript context injection)** ([GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48)): the `first_day_of_week` setting was echoed directly into a JavaScript string literal in the datepicker initialization in `head.php`, with only HTML escaping applied — which does not protect a JavaScript string context. An authenticated administrator could set the value to a payload that breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every authenticated user who loads a page with a datepicker. **Fix:** a new `encode_for_javascript_string()` helper escapes backslashes, quotes, line terminators, and forward slashes before the value is embedded in the script, and `Settings::index()` now validates `first_day_of_week` against the valid `0`–`6` range server-side, rejecting and logging anything else. Thanks to [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) for responsible disclosure. [#1751](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1751)

- **Stored XSS via unescaped `currency_symbol` on public guest invoice/quote pages (CWE-79)** ([GHSA-x4g3-fp78-5gjx](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x4g3-fp78-5gjx)): a duplicate report of the same `format_currency()` escaping gap closed by [GHSA-gpv9-p6gj-238h](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-gpv9-p6gj-238h), scoped specifically to the unauthenticated guest invoice/quote pages. Already fixed by the same single-choke-point `htmlsc()` applied in `number_helper.php`'s `format_currency()`. Thanks to [@medamineelhatimi](https://github.com/medamineelhatimi), [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35), [@crypto-nidh](https://github.com/crypto-nidh) for responsible disclosure. [#1744](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1744)

- **Negative item quantity/price accepted in invoice save, enabling total manipulation** ([GHSA-jvcw-w8pr-j92c](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-jvcw-w8pr-j92c)): invoice/quote item quantities and prices were accepted without a non-negative check, letting an authenticated user drive an invoice's total — and the balance owed — negative or arbitrarily low by entering negative values. **Fix:** item quantity and price are now validated as non-negative before save. Thanks to [@RekhanshRajput](https://github.com/RekhanshRajput) for responsible disclosure. [#1758](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1758). A follow-up makes the invoice and quote save stop after a validation error response, so a refused invoice number, a nameless item or a failed custom-field save no longer lets the rest of the save run in autocommit mode ([#1788](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1788))

- **Clickjacking on guest quote-approval pages in Docker deployments (CWE-1021)** ([GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm)): the bundled Docker nginx configuration did not carry forward the `X-Frame-Options` header set elsewhere in the app for `Guest_Controller`/`Base_Controller` responses, so a Docker deployment's guest-facing quote-approval page could be framed by an attacker's page and tricked into a clickjacked approval. **Fix:** `X-Frame-Options` is now applied directly in `Guest_Controller`/`Base_Controller` rather than relying solely on the reverse-proxy config. Thanks to [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) for responsible disclosure. [#1723](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1723)

- **Gateway-callback payment recording race (TOCTOU, CWE-362 / CWE-367).** The guest Stripe
  (`callback`) and PayPal (`paypal_capture_payment`) endpoints recorded an online payment in
  three separate, non-atomic steps: read `invoice_balance`, check it, then insert into
  `ip_payments`. Two callbacks arriving concurrently for the same invoice, each carrying a
  *distinct* gateway reference (distinct `payment_intent` / `capture_id`, so the existing
  `payment_external_id` dedup matches neither — this is the concurrent variant of the replay
  issue behind [GHSA-6cpc-hr8h-xgr2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-6cpc-hr8h-xgr2)),
  could both pass the balance check before either committed, double-crediting the invoice and
  driving `invoice_balance` negative. **Fix:** `Mdl_Payments::record_external_payment()`
  collapses the guard and the insert into one atomic operation — a single conditional `UPDATE`
  on `ip_invoice_amounts` that only succeeds while `invoice_balance > 0`, serialized by InnoDB
  on that row, followed by an `INSERT IGNORE` so a reference that still raced past a wider
  balance is dropped by the unique `payment_external_id` index rather than erroring. The
  `044_1.7.3.sql` migration adding that index is also repaired in place to make it `UNIQUE`
  (it shipped non-unique), reconciling any duplicate rows recorded during that window without
  deleting history. [#1705](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1705)

- **Payment-amount validation race (TOCTOU, CWE-362 / CWE-367).** `Mdl_Payments::validate_payment_amount()`
  read `invoice_balance` and `Mdl_Payments::save()` inserted the payment row as separate,
  non-atomic steps. Concurrent payment submissions from distinct authenticated admin sessions
  for the same invoice could each read the same stale balance and pass validation before either
  committed, driving the invoice into an overpaid (negative-balance) state. Both admin payment
  entry points (`Payments::form()`, `Ajax::add()`) now serialize on the invoice with a new
  `PaymentCallbackLock` library: a connection-scoped MySQL advisory lock, so a losing submission
  blocks until the winner commits, then re-validates against the now-current balance. **Note on
  scope:** this is distinct from gateway replay deduplication (the unique index on
  `ip_payments.payment_external_id`, shipped in 1.7.3). That index does not exist on
  installations still running the released 1.7.2; this fix does not add it retroactively — it
  only closes the admin-side balance race. Reported by
  [@hariprakash6969-create](https://github.com/hariprakash6969-create).
  [#1756](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1756)

- **PayPal PENDING capture status treated as settled payment (unconfirmed funds):** PayPal can return a `PENDING` status for captures that have not yet settled, indicating that the transaction is in progress but funds have not yet reached the merchant account. The PayPal controller accepted both `COMPLETED` and `PENDING` statuses as valid payment settlement indicators, causing PENDING transactions to be recorded as paid invoices and reducing the customer's outstanding balance before PayPal confirmed settlement. This created reconciliation issues and potential double-charging if a PENDING transaction subsequently failed. **Fix:** only `COMPLETED` captures are now recorded as settled payments through `record_external_payment()`. `PENDING` captures are logged to `merchant_responses` for tracking and audit purposes, but do NOT update the invoice balance or mark the invoice as paid. The customer is notified that their payment is pending settlement, awaiting PayPal webhook confirmation. **Recommendation:** existing deployments should review any invoices paid via PayPal in the last 90 days and verify that PENDING transactions have not been incorrectly marked as settled. Thanks to [@santhoshdodo2721](https://github.com/santhoshdodo2721) for responsible disclosure.

- **Unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive financial data via static-file exposure (CWE-538, CWE-284, CWE-22, CWE-668):** nginx deployments using the project's bundled configuration did not deny direct access to the `/uploads/` subdirectories. The at-rest protection of `uploads/customer_files/`, `uploads/archive/`, `uploads/import/`, and `uploads/temp/` relied on `.htaccess` files containing `Deny from all`, which nginx does not honor. An unauthenticated attacker could directly download raw import CSV files (client names, addresses, payment amounts), archived invoice PDFs (enumerable by date + invoice number), and temporary files, bypassing all application-level access control. **Fix:** explicit `location ^~ /uploads/<subdir>/` deny blocks added to `resources/docker/nginx/invoiceplane.conf`; import CSV files are now deleted immediately after processing (not persisted to disk); archived PDF filenames are randomized (32-hex-character token instead of `YYYY-MM-DD_<name>` pattern) to prevent enumeration. **Recommendation:** existing nginx deployments should upgrade this configuration block and consider moving `uploads/` outside the web root (served only through authenticated PHP endpoints). ([GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m)) Thanks to [@nirtem](https://github.com/nirtem), [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d), and [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0) for responsible disclosure. [#1716](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1716)

- **The Layout controller is no longer routable (follow-up to [GHSA-x2m4-962x-cphw](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x2m4-962x-cphw)):** `Layout` is a helper other controllers call directly but extends `MX_Controller` with public methods, so `/layout/layout/render` answered 200 to a visitor without a session. `_remap()` now answers 404; the direct calls are unaffected. Thanks to [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) and [@yeshwanthmoota](https://github.com/yeshwanthmoota) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-x2m4-962x-cphw](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x2m4-962x-cphw), [#1797](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1797))

- **Object-level authorization missing in `Users::delete()` — peer admins could delete other admins (CWE-639 / CWE-269):** The `Users::delete()` endpoint validated that the *target* user was not the primary administrator, but did not check whether the *acting* user had permission to delete another user's account. A secondary administrator (`user_type=1`, `user_id != 1`) could delete other administrator accounts. The fix adds an `is_primary_administrator()` authorization guard consistent with `form()` and `change_password()`, allowing only the primary admin to delete other users. Sessions are invalidated on delete for immediate privilege revocation. ([GHSA-6r23-8rf2-78h3](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-6r23-8rf2-78h3)) Thanks to [@capivara-research](https://github.com/capivara-research) and [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) for the responsible disclosure. [#1713](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1713)

- **Object-level authorization missing in `Users/Ajax::save_user_client()` — peer admins could assign clients to any user (CWE-862 / CWE-269):** The AJAX endpoint that assigns clients to users lacked authorization checks, allowing any authenticated user to modify another user's client assignments without permission. A secondary administrator could reassign another user's clients, disrupting data isolation. The fix adds the same authorization pattern as the main Users controller: only the primary admin may assign clients to other users; regular users may only modify their own client list. Thanks to [@capivara-research](https://github.com/capivara-research) for the responsible disclosure. [#1714](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1714)

- **Import CSV files are deleted on every submit (follow-up to [GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m)):** the cleanup ran only when at least one file was ticked, so submitting the import form with nothing selected left the uploaded client, invoice and payment CSVs in `uploads/import`. The cleanup now always runs. Thanks to [@nirtem](https://github.com/nirtem), [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) and [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m), [#1798](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1798))

- **SQL operator precedence vulnerability in guest invoice listing — ungrouped OR filters escape client scoping** ([GHSA-w5r4-8w63-c5h2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-w5r4-8w63-c5h2), CWE-639 / CWE-862): The `Mdl_invoices::is_paid()` method uses an ungrouped `filter_or_where()` condition that, when combined with the guest controller's client-scoping `where_in()`, allows the OR to bind more tightly than the AND, leaking invoices from other clients. The SQL evaluates as `WHERE status=4 OR (balance='0.00' AND client_id IN (...))` instead of the intended `WHERE (status=4 OR balance='0.00') AND client_id IN (...)`. Guest users can enumerate invoices from other clients by exploiting the zero-balance or paid-status conditions. The initial fix in [#1715](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1715) wrapped both conditions in `group_start()/group_end()`, but those run immediately against the query builder while `filter_where()`/`filter_or_where()` are deferred by `MY_Model::__call()` and only applied later by `run_filters()` — so the group closed empty and the vulnerability was not actually fixed. [#1717](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1717) corrects this using `filter_group_start()/filter_group_end()`, which defers the grouping into the same queue as the two conditions. **CVSS 5.3** (Medium — Unauthorized Information Disclosure). Thanks to [@d3do-23](https://github.com/d3do-23) and [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) for responsible disclosure.

- **Login rate-limit counter forgery via the shared `ip_login_log` key column (CWE-694):** five different counters (per-account login lockout, login-IP throttle, password-reset IP and email throttles, cron-key throttle) share `ip_login_log.login_name`. The four throttles use namespaced `<prefix>:<sha256>` keys, but the per-account login lockout — and the password-reset token counter — wrote the raw, unvalidated value the client submitted, so an unauthenticated attacker could submit another counter's key (for example `login_ip:<sha256(ip)>`) as an email address or reset token and deliberately fail, locking out a chosen IP, blocking password recovery for an account, or tripping the cron throttle. **Fix:** both counters now use namespaced keys of the same shape (`login_account:<sha256(lower(email))>` and `password_reset_token:<sha256(token)>`), so submitted input can no longer address another counter. Counters keyed the old way are migrated on first use: the row is renamed to its namespaced key and keeps its count and timestamp, so an active lockout survives the upgrade (if both a legacy and a namespaced row exist, the higher count is kept). A password reset also clears such a not-yet-migrated row, so the owner is not locked out after choosing a new password ([#1765](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1765)). Thanks to [@Taxanehh](https://github.com/Taxanehh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-r59m-wgg6-h4pv](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-r59m-wgg6-h4pv))

- **Reset tokens fail closed (follow-up to [GHSA-fwj7-c84x-jvjq](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj7-c84x-jvjq) and [GHSA-5r28-6rw3-25c2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5r28-6rw3-25c2)):** a token row without a stored expiry was accepted forever, and a reset link requested before a password change stayed usable after it. A missing expiry is now treated like a malformed one, and changing a password clears the pending token and its expiry. Thanks to [@baozongwi](https://github.com/baozongwi) and [@ali-iltizar](https://github.com/ali-iltizar) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-fwj7-c84x-jvjq](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj7-c84x-jvjq), [GHSA-5r28-6rw3-25c2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5r28-6rw3-25c2), [#1793](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1793))

- **Missing object-level authorization on the user-client assignment endpoints (CWE-639 / CWE-862):** after `Users/Ajax::save_user_client()` received its primary-administrator-or-self check, the same write semantics remained unguarded in `User_Clients::create()`, `User_Clients::delete()` and `Users::delete_user_client()`. A secondary administrator could grant or revoke any user's client assignments, and — by posting `user_all_clients` for their own account — bulk-assign every client in the system to themselves, gaining read access to every invoice, quote and payment. **Fix:** a shared `Mdl_User_Clients::can_manage_user_clients()` check (primary administrator or the account owner) now guards all three endpoints, including the `user_id` the model saves from POST data; the assignment being deleted must belong to the user in the URL; only the primary administrator may set `user_all_clients`; and the id must be a plain integer (a value such as `2.9` would otherwise be authorized as user 2 but stored as user 3). Independently found and reported again by [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) via the `User_clients::create()`/`delete()` routes. Thanks to [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35), [@dreamer1eh](https://github.com/dreamer1eh), and [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w))

- **Stored XSS via custom field label in validation error alerts (CWE-79 / CWE-116):** `Validator` interpolated the custom field label and error message into the flash alert HTML without escaping, so a label containing markup executed when a validation error was displayed. **Fix:** both are escaped with `htmlsc()` before being formatted into the message. Thanks to [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-xvpx-fwvm-346g](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-xvpx-fwvm-346g))

- **Stored XSS via unescaped `currency_symbol` — 15 remaining view sinks (CWE-79 / CWE-116):** the earlier `currency_symbol` fix escaped the value in the formatting helpers but 15 view templates (invoice and quote item lists, discount inputs, the product and task forms) still echoed the setting raw, so a stored payload executed in administrator and guest sessions. **Fix:** every remaining sink escapes the value on output. Thanks to [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35) and [@medamineelhatimi](https://github.com/medamineelhatimi) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-gpv9-p6gj-238h](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-gpv9-p6gj-238h))

- **Stored XSS in guest payment pages via unescaped payment-gateway settings (CWE-79):** PayPal and Stripe settings (client id, currency, API key) were echoed bare into single-quoted JavaScript string literals on the guest payment pages. Breaking out of a JS string needs no HTML metacharacter, so the `xss_clean()` input filter did not stop it, and the script ran for unauthenticated customers paying an invoice. **Fix:** every value is emitted with `json_encode()` using `JSON_HEX_TAG|JSON_HEX_AMP|JSON_HEX_APOS|JSON_HEX_QUOT` in `guest/views/gateways/paypal.php` and `stripe.php`. Thanks to [@T0x1cG](https://github.com/T0x1cG) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-mp5h-3jcr-f7hm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-mp5h-3jcr-f7hm))

- **Self password change no longer reads a `user_auth_version` that does not exist (follow-up to [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj)):** the self password change in `Users::change_password()` read `$updated_user->user_auth_version`, a column this branch does not have, so it raised an undefined-property warning and stored `0` in the session, and a comment described a check that is not there. The read is removed; the session stays bound to the new password through its credential fingerprint. Thanks to [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0), [@iamharshitgupta](https://github.com/iamharshitgupta) and [@0x0Axlw](https://github.com/0x0Axlw) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3), [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj), [#1766](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1766))

- **Recurring-invoice cron refused when no cron key is configured (follow-up to [GHSA-28fh-2656-wc63](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-28fh-2656-wc63)):** with a blank `cron_key` setting a request without a key compared an empty string with an empty string and was accepted, running the job unauthenticated and bypassing the failed-attempt limiter. An empty configured key is now treated as a wrong key. Thanks to [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-28fh-2656-wc63](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-28fh-2656-wc63), [#1790](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1790))

- **SSRF via `thousands_separator` / `decimal_point` settings and the mPDF footer filename (CWE-918):** the number-format settings and the document filename were concatenated unescaped into HTML that mPDF renders, and mPDF fetches remote resources referenced in that HTML — so a user able to write settings (or a crafted filename) could make the server issue requests to arbitrary hosts. **Fix:** `format_currency()`, `format_amount()` and `format_quantity()` now escape both separators with `htmlsc()`, and the filename in the invoice/quote footer is passed through `htmlspecialchars()`. Thanks to [@fr1d4yy](https://github.com/fr1d4yy) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-x9qq-6v8r-pfcf](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x9qq-6v8r-pfcf), [GHSA-ph5g-ffvw-r5vq](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-ph5g-ffvw-r5vq))

- **Recurring-invoice cron no longer burns an invoice number when it loses the claim (follow-up to [GHSA-hvvh-fjx5-9j55](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hvvh-fjx5-9j55)):** the cron drew the next number from the invoice group before it claimed the recurring invoice, so a run that lost the claim to a concurrent run consumed a number without creating an invoice. The number is now drawn after the claim, inside the same transaction, with the group row locked. Thanks to [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-hvvh-fjx5-9j55](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hvvh-fjx5-9j55))

- **Sessions not invalidated after a password change (CWE-613):** changing or resetting a password only rewrote the bcrypt hash; `User_Controller` re-validated the account's role and active state on each request but nothing tied a session to the password it was created with, so a session opened with the old (possibly compromised) password stayed authorized until it expired — ten days by default. **Fix:** `Mdl_Sessions::auth()` stores an HMAC fingerprint of the password hash in the session (`session_credential_fingerprint()` in `ip_security_helper.php`), and `User_Controller` compares it with the current hash on every request and destroys the session on mismatch. A user changing their own password keeps their current session; every other session of that account ends on its next request. Sessions that predate this fix are bound to the current password on their first request. Two follow-ups: a self password change no longer reads a `user_auth_version` property that does not exist on this branch ([#1766](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1766)), and `Mdl_sessions::invalidate_user_sessions()`, the helper meant to end a user's other sessions, read the session path from a property that does not exist and parsed the session files with `unserialize()`, which cannot read PHP's session file format, so it deleted nothing; it now reads the configured session path and the top-level `user_id` entry directly, and only touches files named like this application's sessions ([#1768](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1768)). Thanks to [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0), [@iamharshitgupta](https://github.com/iamharshitgupta) and [@0x0Axlw](https://github.com/0x0Axlw) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3), [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj))

- **Clickjacking headers are validated before they are sent (follow-up to [GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm)):** the admin, guest and base controllers each sent `X-Frame-Options` straight from the raw `X_FRAME_OPTIONS` value, so an invalid setting (`ALLOWALL`, a typo) produced an invalid header that browsers ignore, and `DENY` still sent a CSP of `frame-ancestors 'self'`. One helper, `security_frame_headers()`, now accepts only `SAMEORIGIN` or `DENY` (anything else falls back to `SAMEORIGIN`) and derives the matching CSP; all three controllers use it, so admin pages now carry the CSP too. Thanks to [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm))

- **`invalidate_user_sessions()` deleted nothing, and now only touches real session files (follow-up to [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj)):** the helper meant to end a user's other sessions read the session path from a property that does not exist and parsed the session files with `unserialize()`, which cannot read PHP's session file format, so no session was ever removed. It now reads the configured session path, only considers files named like this application's sessions (the save path defaults to the shared system temp directory) and reads the top-level `user_id` entry, so text inside another value cannot pass for the owner. Thanks to [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0), [@iamharshitgupta](https://github.com/iamharshitgupta) and [@0x0Axlw](https://github.com/0x0Axlw) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3), [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj), [#1768](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1768))

- **A copy of the session that changes its own password stayed valid (follow-up to [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj)):** the session performing a self password change was re-bound to the new credentials but kept its session id, so a stolen cookie of that same session still worked. The session id is now regenerated and the old session destroyed, so the owner stays logged in and the copy does not. Thanks to [@mkax0](https://github.com/mkax0), [@iamharshitgupta](https://github.com/iamharshitgupta) and [@0x0Axlw](https://github.com/0x0Axlw) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6g-m4fp-7cj3), [GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hw8f-c8c2-g4fj), [#1789](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1789))

- **PayPal capture moved funds before the local invoice checks, and always logged success (CWE-391 / CWE-754 / CWE-841):** `Paypal::paypal_capture_payment()` called `captureOrder()` first and only afterwards checked the invoice (still public, still unpaid, currency, amount, remaining balance). If the invoice changed between order creation and capture — balance raised or lowered, paid another way, cancelled — the customer had already been charged but no payment was recorded, a cancelled invoice ended in an uncaught exception (HTTP 500), and the `ip_merchant_responses` row was written as successful regardless. **Fix:** the order is now read back from PayPal and verified against the current invoice (public, unpaid, same currency, amount equal to the balance) *before* anything is captured; if the check fails nothing is captured and the customer is told to retry. The uncaught post-capture exception is gone, and the merchant response is only logged as successful when the capture was actually recorded — otherwise it is flagged "captured at PayPal, NOT recorded locally" and an error is logged for manual reconciliation. Thanks to [@Ishbarna](https://github.com/Ishbarna) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-m2c5-pmxf-qfh5](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-m2c5-pmxf-qfh5))

- **The balance check only counts the amount of a payment that belongs to the invoice (follow-up to [GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6)):** when a payment is edited, its old amount is added back to the invoice balance before the new amount is checked. The payment was looked up by the posted `payment_id` alone, so naming a payment of a different invoice added that invoice's amount to this one and let an overpayment pass the "cannot exceed the balance" check. The lookup is now limited to the posted invoice, and an unknown id adds nothing. Thanks to [@hariprakash6969-create](https://github.com/hariprakash6969-create) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6))

- **Session cookie pinned to `SameSite=Lax`, and document numbers whitelisted in PDF and XML filenames (follow-ups to [GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm) and [GHSA-54xh-8h4r-4f3r](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-54xh-8h4r-4f3r)):** `sess_samesite` is now set explicitly instead of relying on the library default, so a cross-site framed page cannot ride on the visitor's session. Invoice, quote and Sumex PDF filenames, and the invoice XML filename, now go through `sanitize_document_number_for_filename()` instead of a denylist of `\` and `/`, which let drive letters and other path characters through. Thanks to [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d), [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) and [@yeshwanthmoota](https://github.com/yeshwanthmoota) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-858w-pp5p-wphm), [GHSA-54xh-8h4r-4f3r](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-54xh-8h4r-4f3r))

- **Unauthenticated requests to the payment-gateway controllers trigger outbound API calls; Stripe callback crashes on uninitialized state:** `guest/gateways/stripe/callback/<id>` is reachable without authentication. For any invalid id the Stripe call threw, and the `finally` block then dereferenced `$session` and `$invoice`, which were never assigned, attempted an insert with a NULL `invoice_id` into a NOT NULL column, and ended in an HTTP 500 without the intended redirect — at the cost of one Stripe API call per request. Separately, every request that reached the PayPal controller made a live OAuth token request from the library constructor. **Fix:** the Stripe callback rejects ids that are not a well-formed Checkout Session id before any API call, initialises its state before the `try`, and only writes the merchant response when an invoice was resolved; `PaypalLib` now authorizes lazily, on the first real API call. Thanks to [@Ishbarna](https://github.com/Ishbarna) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-r382-4chp-xj3p](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-r382-4chp-xj3p)) **Follow-up:** a missing invoice key, order id or Checkout Session id on the PayPal/Stripe endpoints (`paypal_create_order`, `paypal_capture_payment`, `create_checkout_session`, `callback`) now answers 404 instead of a PHP error, and the Stripe client is built on first use, so a request refused before any Stripe call no longer fails when no API key is configured. Thanks again to [@Ishbarna](https://github.com/Ishbarna) for responsible disclosure. ([#1829](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1829))
- **Payment-amount validation race (TOCTOU, CWE-362 / CWE-367)** ([GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-c2qp-26qj-6gf6)): Thanks to [@hariprakash6969-create](https://github.com/hariprakash6969-create) for responsible disclosure. [#1756](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1756)
- **PayPal `PENDING` capture treated as settled payment** ([GHSA-w6fv-2f29-rc6g](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-w6fv-2f29-rc6g)): Thanks to [@santhoshdodo2721](https://github.com/santhoshdodo2721) for responsible disclosure. A follow-up records the capture id in the `PENDING` audit row's reference, which is what PayPal reports when the capture settles or is denied, so the row can be reconciled later ([#1772](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1772)). [#1724](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1724)

- **Client and user pickers stop after an empty query (follow-up to [GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88)):** `name_query()` answered an empty query with `[]` and then ran the search with a bare wildcard, appending a second JSON document that listed every active client or user. Both methods now return after the empty response. Thanks to [@PLpaPLpa](https://github.com/PLpaPLpa) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88), [#1791](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1791))
- **SQL injection via string concatenation in the Ajax `having()` clause** ([GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-g7f2-mj3r-xx88)): Thanks to [@PLpaPLpa](https://github.com/PLpaPLpa) for responsible disclosure. [#1630](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1630)
- **Authorization bypass through user-controlled key (IDOR)** ([GHSA-h4xh-4jwc-485r](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-h4xh-4jwc-485r)): Thanks to [@0raN9ewww](https://github.com/0raN9ewww), [@sharma19d](https://github.com/sharma19d) for responsible disclosure. [#1626](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1626)
- **Disabled users can still authenticate** ([GHSA-jw57-6692-jh2q](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-jw57-6692-jh2q)): Thanks to [@mattmumford-git](https://github.com/mattmumford-git) for responsible disclosure. [#1621](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1621)

- **User-client assignment works again (follow-up to [GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w)):** assigning clients to a user, removing an assignment and creating a user with clients selected loaded the model from the wrong module and failed with "Unable to locate the model", so the authorization checks never ran. All five loads now use `user_clients/mdl_user_clients`. Thanks to [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35), [@dreamer1eh](https://github.com/dreamer1eh) and [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w), [#1794](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1794)) **Follow-up:** `Users/Ajax::save_user_client()` also loads the users model that its authorization check calls, so assigning clients to an existing user no longer fails with "Class Mdl_Users not found". ([#1836](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1836))

- **Client assignments of any user readable by a secondary administrator (CWE-639 / CWE-862, follow-up to [GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w)):** the rule "the primary administrator may read or change anyone's client assignments, everybody else only their own" was applied to the endpoints that change assignments but not to the three that list them, so a secondary administrator could read the assignments of the primary administrator or a peer. **Fix:** `users/ajax/load_user_client_table`, `users/ajax/modal_add_user_client` and `user_clients/user/<id>` now apply it, `save_user_client()` shares the same check, and a non-integer user id is refused. Thanks to [@imgolamrabbani](https://github.com/imgolamrabbani) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-ppgp-rvmx-2wp5](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-ppgp-rvmx-2wp5)) ([#1836](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1836))
- **Missing CSRF protection on state-changing delete / logo actions** ([GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf)): Thanks to [@mattmumford-git](https://github.com/mattmumford-git) for responsible disclosure. [#1559](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1559), [#1561](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1561), [#1622](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1622), [#1624](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1624)
- **Sensitive import CSV disclosure via web-accessible import directory** ([GHSA-wv2c-c285-9hrq](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-wv2c-c285-9hrq)): Thanks to [@mattmumford-git](https://github.com/mattmumford-git) for responsible disclosure. [#1623](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1623)
- **Login rate-limit counter forgery via the shared `ip_login_log` key column (CWE-694):** five different counters (per-account login lockout, login-IP throttle, password-reset IP and email throttles, cron-key throttle) share `ip_login_log.login_name`. The four throttles use namespaced `<prefix>:<sha256>` keys, but the per-account login lockout — and the password-reset token counter — wrote the raw, unvalidated value the client submitted, so an unauthenticated attacker could submit another counter's key (for example `login_ip:<sha256(ip)>`) as an email address or reset token and deliberately fail, locking out a chosen IP, blocking password recovery for an account, or tripping the cron throttle. **Fix:** both counters now use namespaced keys of the same shape (`login_account:<sha256(lower(email))>` and `password_reset_token:<sha256(token)>`), so submitted input can no longer address another counter. Counters keyed the old way are not carried over, so active login throttles reset once on upgrade. Thanks to [@Taxanehh](https://github.com/Taxanehh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-r59m-wgg6-h4pv](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-r59m-wgg6-h4pv))
- **Stored XSS in guest payment pages via unescaped payment-gateway settings (CWE-79):** PayPal and Stripe settings (client id, currency, API key) were echoed bare into single-quoted JavaScript string literals on the guest payment pages. Breaking out of a JS string needs no HTML metacharacter, so the `xss_clean()` input filter did not stop it, and the script ran for unauthenticated customers paying an invoice. **Fix:** every value is emitted with `json_encode()` using `JSON_HEX_TAG|JSON_HEX_AMP|JSON_HEX_APOS|JSON_HEX_QUOT` in `guest/views/gateways/paypal.php` and `stripe.php`. Thanks to [@T0x1cG](https://github.com/T0x1cG) and [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-mp5h-3jcr-f7hm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-mp5h-3jcr-f7hm))
- **`encode_for_javascript_string()` did not actually escape JS line terminators:** the fix for [GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48) ([#1751](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1751)) added replacement entries for U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR), but each entry's replacement value was the same raw character as its search key (both characters render as blank whitespace in an editor, so the mistake wasn't visible). The `str_replace()` call was therefore a no-op for both: a `first_day_of_week` value containing either character passed straight through unescaped. Modern JS engines (ES2019+) now permit these characters unescaped inside a string literal, so this is a correctness/robustness bug rather than an active XSS bypass, but it defeats the documented intent of the helper. Replacement values are now the unambiguous escape `"\x20"` instead of a literal character that can be visually confused with the one it's meant to replace. Found while porting the fix to the fork's `prep/v180` branch; no external reporter.

- **Temporary SUMEX XML now has an unpredictable name and owner-only permissions (CWE-73 / CWE-200 / CWE-548):** the 1.7.2 fix moved the file out of `uploads/temp/`, but the name was still `<invoice number>.xml` and the file world-readable, so anyone able to reach `storage/temp/` could guess it. The name now carries 16 random hex characters and the file is created owner-only from the start (a failed write or permission change is reported and no path is handed out). Thanks to [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) and [@mattmumford-git](https://github.com/mattmumford-git) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-65qw-2ppj-gjvm](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-65qw-2ppj-gjvm), [GHSA-583r-4pw9-6rc9](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-583r-4pw9-6rc9), [#1767](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1767))

- **Remaining SUMEX XML fields sanitised; `&` no longer truncates names (CWE-91):** the 1.7.2 fix added `sanitizeXmlText()` but left `item_name`, the company GLN and RCC, the case number, the insured number and the patient AVS number unsanitised, so a control character in any of them still produced a document that is not well-formed; and text assigned through `DOMNode::nodeValue` was cut at an `&`. Those fields are sanitised and text is now added as text nodes. Thanks to [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) and [@yeshwanthmoota](https://github.com/yeshwanthmoota) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-j7f7-999x-v4gx](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-j7f7-999x-v4gx), [#1770](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1770))

- **`verify_csrf_token()` trusted CodeIgniter's CSRF check even for URIs it never checked:** the fix for the "unable to delete an invoice" error (#1694) accepted a POST whose submitted token was `null` on the assumption that CodeIgniter had already validated and consumed it. For a URI in `csrf_exclude_uris` the framework returns early and never touches the token, so a tokenless POST would have been accepted there. The shortcut now applies only to URIs that are not CSRF-excluded; excluded URIs go through the explicit token comparison. Thanks to [@venkatesh2003631](https://github.com/venkatesh2003631) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-mhvh-4j3w-7pvj](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-mhvh-4j3w-7pvj), [#1784](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1784))

- **Stored XSS via unescaped `system_theme` setting (CWE-79, leading to CWE-116 / CWE-20 / CWE-693):** `system_theme` was persisted by `Settings::index()` with no server-side allowlist — unlike `first_day_of_week`, which already has a guard in the same loop — and echoed unescaped by `_theme_asset()` into a double-quoted `href="..."` attribute on 18 views, including the unauthenticated login page, so a value planted by any administrator (not just the primary one) executed in the browser of every visitor, logged in or not. An attribute-breakout payload (`x" onerror="..." x="`) contains no `<` and matches none of `xss_clean()`'s tag- or keyword-gated filters, so the global input filter did not stop it either. **Fix:** `Settings::index()` now validates `system_theme` against the same theme list its own `<select>` is built from, and `_theme_asset()` escapes the value on output as defense-in-depth. Thanks to [@cray4367](https://github.com/cray4367) for responsible disclosure. [#1805](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1805)

### Bug fixes

- **Empty client birthdates are now cleared on MySQL 8 too:** `043_1.7.2.sql` compared the DATE column `client_birthdate` with the literal `'0000-00-00'`, which MySQL 8's default `sql_mode` (`NO_ZERO_DATE`) rejects (error 1525), so on MySQL 8 that cleanup never ran. The 1.7.3 migration now runs the same cleanup comparing the column as text, which works on MySQL 8, MySQL 5.7 and MariaDB. `043_1.7.2.sql` itself is unchanged. Reported and fixed by [@bharath32](https://github.com/bharath32). [#1827](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/issues/1827)

- **Empty `SESS_SAVE_PATH` no longer breaks session startup — fixed in code, not just
  packaging.** 1.7.3 shipped `ipconfig.php.example` with the line commented out, but any
  install that still had `SESS_SAVE_PATH=` in its `ipconfig.php` (an upgrade, or a copy made
  before 1.7.3) stayed broken: `env()` returns a set-but-empty value as `""`, so
  `application/config/config.php` set `$config['sess_save_path'] = ""`, CodeIgniter's
  `Session_files_driver` ran `ini_set('session.save_path', '')` — overriding `php.ini` /
  `php-fpm.d` / the vhost — and session startup failed (`mkdir('')`), so login broke and the
  manual installer stalled on `.../setup/language`. `config.php` now collapses an empty or
  whitespace-only `SESS_SAVE_PATH` to `sys_get_temp_dir()`, exactly matching an unset one; an
  explicit path is unchanged.

- **PayPal `PENDING` capture never wrote its audit row:** the `PENDING` branch added with the fix that stopped recording pending captures as settled payments read `$capture_data` and `$capture_id`, which are only defined inside the `COMPLETED` branch. The invoice id was always empty, so the "pending – awaiting settlement" merchant-response row was never written and PHP raised undefined-variable warnings. The branch now reads the capture itself. No payment is recorded for a pending capture, as before. Thanks to [@santhoshdodo2721](https://github.com/santhoshdodo2721) for responsible disclosure.

- **`encode_for_javascript_string()` did not actually escape JS line terminators:** the fix for [GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48) ([#1751](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1751)) added replacement entries for U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR), but each entry's replacement value was the same raw character as its search key (both characters render as blank whitespace in an editor, so the mistake wasn't visible). The `str_replace()` call was therefore a no-op for both: a `first_day_of_week` value containing either character passed straight through unescaped. Modern JS engines (ES2019+) now permit these characters unescaped inside a string literal, so this is a correctness/robustness bug rather than an active XSS bypass, but it defeats the documented intent of the helper. Replacement values are now the unambiguous escape `"\x20"` instead of a literal character that can be visually confused with the one it's meant to replace. Found while porting the fix to the fork's `prep/v180` branch; no external reporter. [#1760](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1760)

- **Custom public invoice/quote templates in `CUSTOM_TEMPLATES_FOLDER` returned HTTP 500 on the guest view:** `CUSTOM_TEMPLATES_FOLDER` plus the `CUSTOM_INVOICE_TEMPLATES_PUBLIC` / `CUSTOM_QUOTE_TEMPLATES_PUBLIC` allowlists (added for the 1.7.2 RCE hardening) already worked for PDF templates, but a template selected for the guest-facing public view crashed instead of rendering. Two bugs in `application/helpers/template_helper.php`: `get_validated_template_path()` validated the resolved file against `APPPATH . 'views/'` only, so a template that exists solely in `CUSTOM_TEMPLATES_FOLDER` always failed that check and hit `show_error(..., 500)`, even though `render_template_view()` already gives the custom folder precedence; and `render_template_view()` `include`d the custom file from inside a plain function, where `$this` is undefined, so a template copied from the built-in `InvoicePlane_Web.php` (the natural starting point for a custom one) crashed on its `$this->layout->load_view(...)` call. The path check now looks in the custom folder first, matching `render_template_view()`'s precedence, and the include is bound to the controller instance via `Closure::bind()`. Thanks to [@torreirow](https://github.com/torreirow) for reporting and diagnosing both root causes. [#1780](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/issues/1780), [#1781](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1781)

- **Archived invoice PDFs findable again ([#1783](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1783)):** the random archive names introduced for GHSA-qq8q-gf24-576m left no way to match a copy to its invoice, so guests got a new archive file on every view and the archive page filter found nothing. Names are now `<token>_<invoice name>.pdf`.

- **Update check and news now read from the GitHub Releases API ([#1777](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1777), [#1787](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1787)):** the settings page asked the InvoicePlane IDS servers for the latest version and the news. It now reads the latest release and the release list from GitHub, builds the news with DOM APIs instead of HTML strings, and keeps the IDS hosts as a fallback. Every request is bounded by one shared 8 second timeout so a stalled request reaches its fallback, and a legacy news answer that is not a list moves on to the next host or shows the failed state. Thanks to [@sabinich](https://github.com/sabinich) for the change.

- **Guests could list their own draft invoices in the paid listing ([#1769](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1769)):** a draft has a `0.00` balance, so it matched the `balance = 0.00` condition of the paid listing, and the guest-visibility restriction was only applied in some of the listings. Guests never see drafts or cancelled invoices in the detail view; every listing is now scoped the same way.

- **Stripe callback keeps the refusal message ([#1773](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1773)):** the specific message set for a duplicate payment intent, an invoice that is already paid, or a currency or amount mismatch was overwritten with the generic "payment failed" text, so the guest never learned why the payment was refused.

- **Lockout counter shared between spellings of an address (follow-up to [GHSA-cjwm-qx8w-hrq2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-cjwm-qx8w-hrq2) and [GHSA-hcxg-3465-jc8m](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hcxg-3465-jc8m)):** the failed-login counter was keyed on the submitted email text while the database matches emails case- and trailing-space-insensitively, so a locked-out account could be reached through another spelling with a fresh counter. The submitted address is resolved to the stored spelling before the counter is read. Thanks to [@polybjorn](https://github.com/polybjorn), [@Char0n1507](https://github.com/Char0n1507) and [@yeshwanthmoota](https://github.com/yeshwanthmoota) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-cjwm-qx8w-hrq2](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-cjwm-qx8w-hrq2), [GHSA-hcxg-3465-jc8m](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-hcxg-3465-jc8m), [#1796](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1796))

- **Pager URLs are encoded ([#1774](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1774)):** the base URL of the list pager was printed into `href` attributes without HTML encoding.

- **Client assignment refuses a non-integer user id (follow-up to [GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w)):** `Users/Ajax::save_user_client()` authorised `user_id=2.5` as the acting user 2 through an `(int)` cast, and the INT column stored it as user 3, so a peer administrator could assign clients to another account. Only digit-only ids are accepted now. Thanks to [@Shad0w35](https://github.com/Shad0w35), [@dreamer1eh](https://github.com/dreamer1eh) and [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-5rqm-w9p8-gp7w), [#1795](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1795))

- **Warnings reach the log ([#1782](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1782)):** CodeIgniter 3's logger has no WARNING level, so `log_message('warning', ...)` was discarded, including blocked SVG uploads and the login, password-reset and cron rate-limit events. `MY_Log` now writes them at the production threshold.

- **"Remove logo" works again (follow-up to [GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf)):** the POST buttons were wrapped in their own form inside the settings form; browsers drop a nested form, so the click saved the settings and the logo stayed. The buttons now post the enclosing form to `remove_logo` with `formaction`. Thanks to [@mattmumford-git](https://github.com/mattmumford-git) for responsible disclosure. ([GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-qx8h-35wf-cgqf), [#1792](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1792))

## [1.7.3] - 2026-08-29

### Thank you

Thanks to [@0xMoError-22](https://github.com/0xMoError-22) and [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh)
for responsibly disclosing the issues resolved in this release.

### Security Vulnerability Summary

| Vulnerability | Severity | Security Advisory (GHSA) | Reported By | Fixed In |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Horizontal privilege escalation via email takeover in `Users::form()` | High | [Incomplete Authorization Remediation in Users::form() Enables Primary Administrator Account Takeover](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-77hm-22wp-96wp) | [@0xMoError-22](https://github.com/0xMoError-22) | [#1689](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1689) |
| Primary-administrator role downgrade via `user_type` (privilege destruction, CWE-269) | High | Same root cause as [GHSA-77hm-22wp-96wp](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-77hm-22wp-96wp) | [@0xMoError-22](https://github.com/0xMoError-22) | [#1697](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1697) |
| Stored XSS via `first_day_of_week` setting (JavaScript context injection) | — | [GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/security/advisories/GHSA-x3r7-qm3m-hc48) | [@Suraj-Siddharudh](https://github.com/Suraj-Siddharudh) | [#1751](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1751) |

### Security fixes

- [#1689](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1689) — **Horizontal privilege escalation via email takeover:** PR #1638 fixed password-change authorization (IDOR), but left the email field unprotected. A secondary administrator (`user_type=1`, `user_id != 1`) could edit the primary administrator's email address through the user form, then use password recovery to take over the account. `Users::form()` now validates that only the primary administrator can edit `user_id=1`, and `user_email` is included in `PRIMARY_ADMIN_LOCKED_FIELDS` (defense-in-depth). Thanks to [@0xMoError-22](https://github.com/0xMoError-22) for the responsible disclosure.
- [#1697](https://github.com/InvoicePlane/InvoicePlane/pull/1697) — **Primary-administrator role downgrade via `user_type` (privilege destruction, CWE-269):** the same missing object-level authorization in `Users::form()` also let a secondary administrator rewrite the primary administrator's `user_type` to `2` (guest / read-only) — destroying the root account's privilege, revoking its sessions, and locking the legitimate owner out. The `user_id=1` isolation guard added for the email fix already closes this vector at the controller. This release hardens it further: the `Mdl_Users::save()` data layer now uses `PRIMARY_ADMIN_LOCKED_FIELDS` to strip privilege- and identity-bearing fields (`user_type`, `user_active`, `user_psalt`, `user_email`, `user_password`) from any write targeting `user_id=1` that does not originate from the primary administrator's own session, and the scattered `user_id == 1` checks in `Users::form()`, `Users::delete()` and `Users::change_password()` are consolidated behind a single `Mdl_Users::is_primary_administrator()` predicate so future mutation paths cannot forget the boundary. Thanks to [@0xMoError-22](https://github.com/0xMoError-22) for the responsible disclosure.

### Documentation / configuration

- **Empty `SESS_SAVE_PATH` breaks session startup and stalls the installer — clarified in `ipconfig.php` and the docs:** the `env()` helper treats a set-but-empty variable as a real value, so an `SESS_SAVE_PATH=` line (as previously shipped in `ipconfig.php.example`) makes InvoicePlane force PHP's `session.save_path` to an empty string, overriding any value from `php.ini` / `php-fpm.d` / the vhost. No session can then be written: login fails and manual installs get stuck on `.../setup/language` (setup progress is stored in the session), often with no log output. The `files` session driver logs `mkdir(): Invalid path` and `Configured save path '' is not a directory`. `ipconfig.php.example` now ships the line commented out (so the `sys_get_temp_dir()` fallback applies) with guidance to set an explicit absolute path outside the web root, and a warning against `/tmp` on systemd distros where `PrivateTmp=true` and `systemd-tmpfiles` wipe it. **Existing installs:** edit `ipconfig.php` and either set `SESS_SAVE_PATH` to a real writable directory or remove the empty line. `README.md` and `.github/docs/CONTAINER_DEPLOYMENT.md` updated to match.

## [1.7.2] - 2026-07-17

InvoicePlane 1.7.2 is a **security-focused release**. It resolves every vulnerability
responsibly disclosed against v1.7.0 / v1.7.1 and hardens the application, session handling,
and container tooling throughout. **If you run v1.7.0 or v1.7.1, upgrade immediately** — this
release fixes a critical (CVSSv3 9.9) Remote Code Execution vulnerability.
